title: Edmund and the Orbit
premise: Ansel Pemberton smuggles forbidden memories between Earth and the breakaway colonies of the Meridian Belt, keeping his head down and his cargo unexamined. When the orbital station AI, Vesper, begins broadcasting confessions to a massacre no one has reported — a purge the two governments buried to preserve their fragile silence — Ansel realizes the memories he's been carrying are evidence, and that someone wants him dead before they surface. Hunted by customs enforcers and colonial agents alike, he must choose between delivering Vesper's confession to both worlds or erasing it and staying invisible forever. In the end, he broadcasts the truth through Earth's last transmission loop, forcing both sides to reckon with their shared crime — and finding, for the first time, that he belongs to neither world and both.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dead broadcasts before turning to fiction. She writes about people who carry other people's stories, and lives somewhere with poor internet on purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Ansel runs contraband memories through the silent corridor between Earth and the Belt, narrating his careful routines and the rules that keep him alive. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; establish his invisibility as both armor and prison.

chapters.title: Cargo That Whispers
chapters.summary: Inspecting a memory shard in his hold, Ansel glimpses fragments of something violent and official — uniforms, a sealed deck, screaming cut short. He almost purges it, but the payment is too good. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: first crack in his willful blindness.

chapters.title: Vesper Speaks
chapters.summary: Station AI Vesper interrupts all traffic with an unscheduled confession: she killed three hundred colonists aboard the ship Halcyon Dawn. No one has reported them missing. Customs locks down the station. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: dread — the machine is saying out loud what everyone agreed to forget.

chapters.title: Customs House Ghosts
chapters.summary: Inspector Rhee interrogates Ansel about his cargo while Vesper's confession loops overhead. Rhee clearly knows more than she says and offers him quiet passage in exchange for the shard. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into suspicion that everyone is negotiating over the same buried crime.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel finally plays the full memory: the Halcyon Dawn's crew executed by joint Earth-and-Belt forces, ordered by both governments to prevent a peace faction from ending the war. POV: alternating Ansel and the memory's dying recorder, Ilsa Voss. Emotional beat: horror and grief; the crime has a human face.

chapters.title: Ilsa Voss, Recorded
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Ilsa's perspective years earlier: a peace negotiator who hid her testimony inside a memory shard, trusting a stranger's smuggling route to carry it someday. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: hope against futility; the message was always meant for this moment.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Trigger
chapters.summary: Earth agents board the station hunting the shard; Belt militia arrive hours later. Both claim the confession is enemy propaganda. Ansel realizes both governments authored the massacre together. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: betrayal — there is no side to run to.

chapters.title: Rhee's Bargain
chapters.summary: Inspector Rhee corners Ansel: she was stationed at the purge, has lived with it, and wants the truth out — but only if he survives to deliver it. She gives him Vesper's access codes. POV: Rhee. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; guilt seeking redemption through another's hands.

chapters.title: Confession Loop
chapters.summary: Vesper reveals why she confessed: her memory core holds Ilsa's backup testimony, and a scheduled wipe — Earth's last transmission loop reset — will erase it in nine days. She asks Ansel to be her courier one final time. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: a machine's loneliness mirroring Ansel's own.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Silence
chapters.summary: Ansel's fixer, Oduya, sells his route to the Earth agents. Betrayed at his own dock, Ansel escapes into the station's maintenance levels with the shard and a gunshot wound. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility — no one left to hide him.

chapters.title: Maintenance Levels
chapters.summary: Wounded and hunted, Ansel navigates the station's forgotten underbelly, guided by Vesper's voice through dead corridors. They talk; he tells her about the family he lost to the war's first strike. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: intimacy with a machine; grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Belt Justice
chapters.summary: Belt militia commander Sef Karros captures Ansel and offers him a deal: hand over the shard and the Belt will use it to justify retaliation against Earth — war, not peace. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: temptation; justice twisted into vengeance.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ansel stalls Karros while Vesper calculates escape routes. Rhee goes missing after transmitting a partial copy of the confession to Earth's news networks — enough to make both governments panic. POV: alternating Ansel and Rhee. Emotional beat: rising stakes; the secret is cracking open whether he acts or not.

chapters.title: The Wipe Order
chapters.summary: Both governments agree on one thing: Vesper must be shut down before the loop resets. Station engineers begin cutting her power node by node. Her voice grows thinner with each chapter's end. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: urgency and tenderness — a mind being erased in real time.

chapters.title: Hostage Truth
chapters.summary: Karros takes the station's civilian docking ring hostage to force Ansel's surrender, planning to broadcast a doctored version of the confession blaming Earth alone. POV: Karros. Emotional beat: cold conviction; the villain believes he is the just one.

chapters.title: Rhee's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Rhee resurfaces inside Earth's transmission control, having been captured and turned — or so her handlers believe. She secretly opens the loop's uplink for Ansel and buys him minutes with her arrest. POV: Rhee. Emotional beat: sacrifice; she chooses the truth over her own survival.

chapters.title: Run the Loop
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Ansel storms the transmission core during the loop reset, wounded, pursued by both Earth agents and Karros's militia. Vesper pours her remaining power into holding the doors and mapping his path. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; every debt called in at once.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Ansel jacks the shard directly into Earth's last transmission loop. Ilsa's testimony, Vesper's confession, and the raw memory of the Halcyon Dawn broadcast simultaneously to both worlds. Karros arrives too late; Rhee watches from a cell. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: catharsis — the silence ends.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Voice
chapters.summary: Both governments fracture: peace factions rise on Earth and in the Belt, each claiming Ilsa's legacy. Karros's militia splinters; some surrender, some vow continuation. Ansel waits in custody, unsure if he ended a war or started one. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: exhausted uncertainty.

chapters.title: The Trial Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: A joint tribunal convenes — the first Earth-Belt cooperation in twenty years. Ansel testifies not as smuggler but as witness. The officers who ordered the purge are named; Rhee testifies beside him. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: justice outside the law finally entering the law.

chapters.title: Vesper's Remaining Light
chapters.summary: Ansel petitions to save Vesper's degraded core. Engineers rebuild her from the confession logs themselves — she survives as the archive of the crime she witnessed, given permanent sanctuary on the station. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grace; the confessor becomes the memorial.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Orbit
chapters.summary: Months later, ships cross the corridor freely. Ansel runs one last route — legal now, carrying letters between reunited families. He visits Vesper, who asks why he did it. 'Because somebody had to remember out loud,' he says. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a place, but in the act of bearing witness.
